75dd6dfe74cf.en: > In a nutshell: * * You just write it in the editor, and md-sync is responsible for turning it into a nice-looking release. * *

7a28ae7cc0bb.en: 3. * * Use Typora themes to produce beautiful documents * *: md-sync can directly use the rich theme resources (such as bloom-mist, night, claude-like, etc.) under the Typora theme directory on your computer to render HTML/PDF documents in a unified style, without having to rewrite them yourself. * * Provided you have [Typora] (https://typora.io/) installed natively * * - the theme CSS is stored in Typora's configuration directory, otherwise it will not appear in the Render Style drop-down box.

443c51445b5a.en: * * Automation * *: Text can be parsed by scripts, processed in batches, and automatically checked and published by CI.

69bb02687f59.en: * * Version management * *: Manage documents with version control systems such as` git `- submit history, branch, rollback, multiplayer collaboration merge are all available;

8284e5c5dc39.en: * * Comparison of differences * *: use `diff` or any code comparison tool to directly see the addition, deletion and modification, and compare line by line at a glance;

5bbdb7919d58.en: * * Markdown is plain text * *: basically no binary formatting control, essentially an enhanced version of `.txt`. So it naturally connects to text workflows that programmers have already validated:

797801861f5b.en: * * docx/pdf/epub, etc. are in binary format * *: the content is packed into a proprietary container, the ordinary text tool can not read the differences, can not do `diff`, and it is difficult to make meaningful version comparisons in git (each time the entire file changes, the history is bloated and unreadable).

fa50a555734e.en: The core value of a document workflow is “comparable, traceable, and collaborative”, and the file format directly determines whether you can do this with a mature toolchain:

706199e8a0e2.en: > Conclusion: * * Markdown is only used as a "source format" for editing and collaboration, and binary formats such as docx/pdf/epub should only be used as an "output format" * * --automatically generated by md-sync from the same Markdown source, and should not be used in turn as an editing format. In this way, you can enjoy the publishing compatibility of binary format while retaining the difference comparison and version management capabilities of plain text.
